title: Three models of big data governance: A comparative analysis of privacy policies of contact tracing apps in China, Singapore, and Germany
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and City University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Three models of big data governance: A comparative analysis of privacy policies of contact tracing apps in China, Singapore, and Germany
detail.abstract: The COVID-19 outbreak has spawned a global boom in big data governance worldwide regarding the rollout of contact tracing apps (CTAs). Governments face the dilemma of balancing enhancing governance efficiency to curb the pandemic and protecting citizens’ data privacy. This comparative study examines how China, Singapore, and Germany, three exemplary countries in launching CTAs, address this dilemma in their big data governance process. We first propose a dialectical “legal-technical” framework to articulate the interplay of data protection laws and surveillance technologies in shaping big data governance. We then apply this analytical framework to examine the privacy policies of CTAs in each country. We articulate three big data governance models representing different trade-offs in governance efficiency and data privacy: a centralized and intrusive model in China, a decentralized and unintrusive model in Germany, and a semi-centralized and semi-intrusive model in Singapore. Our findings contribute to a nuanced discussion of adopting information and communication technology in big data governance in post-pandemic societies.

title: Digital Context and Manufacturing Servitization: Evidence from UK Manufacturing
affiliations: Swansea University and Cardiff University

detail.title: Digital Context and Manufacturing Servitization: Evidence from UK Manufacturing
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the impact of digital contexts, specifically digital infrastructure, digital capabilities, digital facilities, and e-commerce engagement, on the servitization strategies of UK manufacturing. Using firm-level panel data, the study examines how different dimensions of digitalization influence manufacturing firms' propensity to purchase Knowledge-Intensive Business Services (KIBS) and import services. Our findings demonstrate that digital infrastructure, digital facilities, and e-commerce engagement facilitates external KIBS usage and service imports, while internal digital capabilities, such as employing ICT specialists, can result in sustainable internalization of KIBS, reducing reliance on external sources. We further explore how the manufacturing technology level influences such findings. The study advances the literature on digital servitization by providing nuanced insights into how the four dimensions of digital contexts mediate servitization. These insights inform managerial strategies and public policies aimed at optimizing digital investments and supporting servitization initiatives, particularly in digitally underserved regions.

title: Traffic Efficiency or Public Transport Priority? Evaluating the Impact of Removing Exclusive Bus Lanes in Beijing
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Traffic Efficiency or Public Transport Priority? Evaluating the Impact of Removing Exclusive Bus Lanes in Beijing
detail.abstract: Exclusive bus lanes have been implemented to prioritize public transport in urban areas. However, with the increasing diversification of urban travel modes, many such lanes remain underutilization, becoming potential bottlenecks that limit improvements in overall traffic efficiency. To empirically assess the traffic effects of underperforming exclusive bus lanes, this study evaluates the policy intervention of removing exclusive bus lanes on the 2nd Ring Road in Beijing as a quasi-natural experiment. Using large-scale ride-hailing order data and a Propensity Score Matching-Difference-in-Differences (PSM-DID) method, we evaluated the policy effects across temporal and spatial dimensions. The results reveal significant heterogeneous effects during morning and evening peak periods, as well as both temporal and spatial spillover effects. Specifically, during the early stages of peak periods, the elimination of exclusive bus lane can substantially improve roadway utilization efficiency, although no significant change was observed in total ride-hailing trip volume. Furthermore, policy effectiveness depends on the intensity and spatiotemporal distribution of travel demand. These findings indicate the need for flexible demand management strategies to achieve a dynamic balance between road resource utilization and sustainable urban mobility.

title: Integrating Cultural Considerations into Psychosocial Mentorship Programs: A Systematic Review of Strategies for Diverse Workforces
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and MacEwan University, School of Business

detail.title: Integrating Cultural Considerations into Psychosocial Mentorship Programs: A Systematic Review of Strategies for Diverse Workforces
detail.abstract: Organizations increasingly acknowledge that mentoring is not a universal process but a culturally embedded practice that shapes trust, communication, and identity. Drawing on 25 empirical studies published between 2000 and 2024, we develop a Cultural Ecosystem Model of Mentorship (CEM) that integrates cultural competence training, culturally attuned matching, contextualized goal-setting, and structured reflection as interlocking strategies. Rather than treating culture as a peripheral factor, the CEM conceptualizes it as a designed subsystem that links macro-level norms, meso-level program artifacts, and micro-level mentor–mentee exchanges through continuous feedback loops. This synthesis advances Social Exchange Theory by introducing cultural reciprocity norms, extends Cultural Psychology by positioning mentors as active schema mediators, and adapts socio-technical systems thinking to embed culture within organizational design. The model also bridges to HRM and industrial relations by showing how culturally responsive mentoring can strengthen retention, trust, and collective voice across diverse workforce segments, including gig work and unionized sectors. For practice, the article outlines a managerial roadmap and boundary conditions for designing culturally responsive mentoring, while for scholarship it proposes a future research agenda emphasizing longitudinal dyadic studies, social network analyses of cultural brokers, participatory action research, and trials of AI-mediated coaching. Together, these contributions position culturally responsive mentoring as both a theoretical extension and a practical blueprint for inclusive workforce development.

title: From promotion to practice: How does ESG disclosure policy shape tangible green investment practices
affiliations: Hong Kong Polytechnic University and Hong Kong Polytechnic University

detail.title: From promotion to practice: How does ESG disclosure policy shape tangible green investment practices
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the effects and underlying mechanisms of voluntary and mandatory ESG disclosure policies on firms’ tangible green investment. We find that under the voluntary ESG disclosure policy, affected firms improve the quality of green building outcomes along the intensive margin by 5.6%. In contrast, under the mandatory ESG disclosure policy, firms increase the quantity of green investments along the extensive margin by 22% and improve quality along the intensive margin by 15.5%. Further analysis shows that impacts vary across firms due to peer pressure, arbitrage, and signaling effect: Firstly, firms face greater reputational and market pressure after ESG disclosures become mandatory, they raise the opportunity cost of not investing green, pushing firms to invest more to maintain legitimacy and competitiveness; Secondly, firms with fewer financial or capability constraints can exploit the increased noise and disclosure from less capable peers under mandatory ESG disclosures, creating a return differential on green investment; Lastly, mandatory ESG disclosure is interpreted as a credible policy signal by firms with long-term orientation and stronger governance, with stable boards expect sustained policy and respond by increasing green investment. In addition, we examine the green building premiums across different types and uncover evidence of the brand spillover effect around 2% to 3%, whereby the presence of green buildings enhances the value of nearby properties under the same brand and find that firms tend to adopt decentralized yet locally clustered portfolio strategies in their green building investments, forming small spatial clusters dispersed across the city.

title: Can Generative AI Help Humans Make Better Decisions? - Comparing LLMs’ Predictions of Human Irrationality
affiliations: Sejong University, Sejong University and Kyungil University

detail.title: Can Generative AI Help Humans Make Better Decisions? - Comparing LLMs’ Predictions of Human Irrationality
detail.abstract: The research was conducted to examine whether generative AI could assist in human decision-making. We conducted an experimental study using two scenarios -- Ultimatum Game and Framing Effect scenarios -- to determine whether generative AIs can make rational decisions unlike humans, and whether they view humans as rational decision makers. The results of the analysis showed that generative AIs made rational decisions differently depending on the scenario. Specifically, in the ultimatum game scenario, generative AIs were more likely than humans to make a rational choice to accept an unfair offer for economic gain. In contrast, in the framing effect scenario, generative AI preferred more uncertain choices in negative frames (as opposed to positive frames), similar to humans. Furthermore, generative AI generally predicted that humans would make rational or irrational decisions in both scenarios in a direction consistent with their own choices. Taken together, the results suggest that generative AI is not a better decision maker than humans as it does not always choose the rational alternative and does not recognize that humans can make irrational decisions based on context and emotion. This suggests that generative AI is limited in its ability to proactively detect and advise humans on possible irrational decisions in the future. To generalize the results of the study, we included various generative AI models beyond ChatGPT, which have been used in previous studies, and considered the characteristics of decision makers, such as knowledge level and culture, whose behavior is predicted by AI.

title: Bundling Against Learning
affiliations: and Stanford Graduate School of Business

detail.title: Bundling Against Learning
detail.abstract: A monopolist sells multiple goods to an uninformed buyer. The buyer chooses to learn any one-dimensional linear signal of their values for the goods, anticipating the seller's mechanism. The seller designs an optimal mechanism, anticipating the buyer's learning choice. In a generalized Gaussian environment, we show that every equilibrium has vertical learning where the buyer's posterior means are comonotonic, and every equilibrium is outcome-equivalent to nested bundling where the seller offers a menu of nested bundles. In equilibrium, the buyer learns more about a higher-tier good, resulting in a higher posterior variance on the log scale.

title: Are Industry Climate Alliances Cartels?
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley - Haas School of Business and Harvard University - Business School (HBS)

detail.title: Are Industry Climate Alliances Cartels?
detail.abstract: We study the anticompetitiveness and effectiveness of industry net-zero alliances—collective commitments by firms within an industry to achieve net-zero emissions—focusing on U.S. airlines. These alliances aim to enhance environmental outcomes through coordination, but raise antitrust concerns. Using airline ticket data, we find no evidence of collusion: alliance members do not raise prices or restrict output compared to non-members, even in routes they collectively dominate. However, firm-year analyses reveal no improvement in emissions or environmental performance. Our findings highlight a paradox: net-zero alliances are "cheap talk alliances"—neither collusive nor effective—potentially because antitrust concerns constrain meaningful coordination.

title: Direct Flights, Trade and Specialization
affiliations: Tecnológico de Monterrey and Harvard University

detail.title: Direct Flights, Trade and Specialization
detail.abstract: We leverage geographic discontinuities in international air travel costs to show that regular direct connections between countries enable them to trade, especially in specialized products. Back-of-the-envelope calculations suggest that the effect of direct flights at this margin could account for up to 1.6% of world trade. While direct flights do not affect the shipping cost of goods, they do enable bilateral business travel. Countries with stronger direct air connections tend to specialize away from each other's baseline comparative advantages. These findings suggest that the possibility of conducting business in person remains critical for bilateral trade and influences countries' patterns of specialization.

title: The Protection of Indigenous Knowledge in Africa

detail.title: The Protection of Indigenous Knowledge in Africa
detail.abstract:
This book provides a comprehensive contemporary and timely account of the protection of indigenous knowledge in Africa by examining issues such as the nature of indigenous knowledge as part of indigenous property and as the fulcrum of indigenous communities in Africa. Acknowledging the centrality of the members of communities of origin in the production and reproduction of indigenous knowledge, this book discusses options to manage the tension between members of the community, communities of origin and their political community.

Furthermore, the book abandons the conceptual distinction between ‘negative’ and ‘positive’ protection and turns towards a subject consideration of indigenous Scientific and Technical Indigenous Knowledge (STIK); indigenous heritage; indigenous designs indigenous music; indigenous audio-visual, indigenous signs expressions and terms as well as the indigenous literary works that are examined within the context of case studies of the indigenous knowledge human and peoples’ rights. The book concludes hat Africa’s modest record of the protection of indigenous knowledge must factor in its extensive use as the foundation of Africa’s entertainment industry and recommends a tripod of ‘community’ ‘participation’ and ‘reward as principles of effective protection. Building on the 2017 title of ‘The Protection of Traditional Cultural Expressions in Africa” this book adopts a mixed method of a legal pluralistic account of indigenous knowledge; using intellectual property as a lens to view indigenous knowledge and a cultural production account of indigenous knowledge and will be useful to intellectual property lawyers; sociologists; economists; Africanists; innovation law and policy specialists and legal practitioners.

title: Evolving Strategic Partnership: Analyzing EU-India Bilateral Defense Cooperation and Institutional Mechanisms for Enhanced Security Collaboration
affiliations: ESPIRIDI LLP

detail.title: Evolving Strategic Partnership: Analyzing EU-India Bilateral Defense Cooperation and Institutional Mechanisms for Enhanced Security Collaboration
detail.abstract: This research critically examines the evolving defence cooperation between the European Union (EU) and India, with particular emphasis on prominent institutional mechanisms, namely the European Defence Fund (EDF), Permanent Structured Cooperation (PESCO), and the Organisation for Joint Armament Cooperation (OCCAR). Employing Neoliberal Institutionalism as the guiding theoretical framework, the research elucidates how these multilateral instruments underpin joint capability development, technological collaboration, and operational interoperability. The analysis juxtaposes the institutionalised efficiency of EU defence frameworks against the systemic procurement challenges confronting India, such as bureaucratic delays and limited indigenous manufacturing capacity. By identifying key impediments to bilateral cooperation, including regulatory and procedural disparities, the study offers strategic foresight aimed at reinforcing institutional integration and promoting sustainable defence partnerships. The findings underscore the significance of institutional reforms and regulatory alignment in strengthening strategic autonomy and enhancing mutual security interests within a multipolar Indo-Pacific context.

title: Surrogate-model-based real-time dispatch optimization of SOFCs in microgrids considering degradation
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology and Huazhong University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Surrogate-model-based real-time dispatch optimization of SOFCs in microgrids considering degradation
detail.abstract: With the increasing role of solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) in microgrids, real-time economic dispatch faces significant challenges due to complex transient dynamics and current-driven degradation. There is a pressing need for methods that can both preserve SOFC response characteristics and ensure long-term reliability during dispatch. To this end, this study first develops a surrogate model that captures transient response features while remaining suitable for real-time scheduling. Degradation induced by stack current variations is then incorporated into the dispatch formulation to explicitly account for lifetime impact. On this basis, to tackle the optimization problem involving nonlinear dynamics, operational targets and constraints, and load stochasticity, a safe reinforcement learning framework with dual Lagrangian multipliers is proposed: one is used to regulate grid reliance and power imbalance, while the other enforces degradation targets. Case studies show that the surrogate model enables accurate dynamics reproduction, while the dual-multiplier strategy achieves balanced performance under uncertainty. Results reveal clear cost–degradation trade-offs across different degradation targets, consistent positive correlation within single training runs, and performance sensitivity to both degradation limits and load profiles. Comparative analysis further confirms that neglecting dynamics or degradation leads to optimistic cost estimates and the inability to effectively track and mitigate degradation.

title: RECOGNIZING UNPAID LABOR IN FINANCIAL AI
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: RECOGNIZING UNPAID LABOR IN FINANCIAL AI

keywords: AI financial platforms JEL Codes: D14

detail.abstract: Most financial tools like Credit Karma or Mint are built for people with steady jobs, regular paychecks, and traditional credit histories. But many underrepresented diasporas such as gig workers, immigrant families, and first-gen students, don’t conform to the workings of traditional financial tools. The same generic tools can’t recognize the economic value of unpaid labor. For example, Maria-an immigrant mom- works 2 jobs and takes care of her kids for over 30 hours a week, but Mint and Credit Karma only take her paychecks and spending into account. Sam, a gig worker, earns different amounts of money each week, causing his income to be extremely unpredictable. Credit Karma and Mint don’t know how to adjust for that, so their advice might be off or confusing when his income goes up and down. Priya, a first-gen college student, helps pay for her family’s expenses while studying full-time. Most financial tools don’t understand how stressful that is or why she might choose to spend money on her family instead of saving for herself. Our new AI-based financial tool proposed in this paper takes everything into account. It understands the value of unpaid labor, notices income changes, and gives unique advice that fits everyone’s financial situations. For Maria, it sees her childcare as real work. For Sam, it helps him manage income ups and downs. For Priya, it helps her plan around family responsibilities while still being able to pay off student debt. This tool shows that financial advice can be more fair and personal when we stop ignoring the invisible work people do. AI can help make financial planning smarter and more inclusive, especially for people who are often left out of the system.

title: In Search for Persistence and Asymmetry: Dynamic Financial Market Effects of ECB Unconventional Policy Announcements
affiliations: WHU Otto Beisheim Graduate School of Management and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: In Search for Persistence and Asymmetry: Dynamic Financial Market Effects of ECB Unconventional Policy Announcements
detail.abstract: We examine the persistence of and asymmetry in the financial market effects of ECB unconventional policy. Using local projections, we estimate impulse response functions for benchmark interest rates of four major euro area economies in response to unconventional policy shocks. We find the financial market effects of ECB unconventional policies are not uniformly persistent. There is heterogeneity in the transmission of ECB forward guidance across the euro area, with persistent effects for the core economies and impersistent effects for the periphery economies. We find the signalling channel of ECB quantitative easing does not have persistent effect. There is some asymmetry in the effects of easing and tightening policy shocks, with tightening shocks being more persistent.

title: The effectiveness of safety interventions addressed to diverse groups: a systematic review
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Kingston University

detail.title: The effectiveness of safety interventions addressed to diverse groups: a systematic review
detail.abstract: The goal of this systematic review is to analyze the types and effectiveness of the interventions aimed at increasing safety and reducing workplace hazards of diverse workers. A search was conducted in three Psychological relevant databases: Web of Science, Scopus and PsycInfo. A total of 1079 unique sources were screened. After applying the inclusion criteria and updating the search, a total of 23 papers were selected. We extracted and systematized data filling in a form with specific information about each study. The included studies were published between 2003 and 2023. They were mainly conducted in the United States, followed by Australia, Bangladesh, Canada, Gambia, India, Qatar, and South Africa. Most of the interventions targeted immigrant and ethnic minority groups, followed by young and/or older workers, women, mixed groups (women and young/older workers; and workers from low-wage countries. Nineteen were quasi-experimental studies, 3 were randomized control trials and 1 was an observational study. Intervention effectiveness was measured in different ways, for instance, in terms of knowledge acquisition and transfer, hazard identification and reduction, and improvements in safety behaviors. The findings show that safety interventions are more effective when tailored to the specific needs of diverse workers. In many cases, interventions yield more positive results when trainers from the target group were involved. However, these tailored safety interventions have only targeted a few diverse groups, overlooking the specific needs of other protected workers. These findings can guide the design and development of future safety interventions.

title: The Evolution of Behavioral Economics in Policy Design: A Critical Review (2015-2025)
affiliations: SOLAV

detail.title: The Evolution of Behavioral Economics in Policy Design: A Critical Review (2015-2025)

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This research did not involve human or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
Purpose: This paper provides a critical synthesis of the key developments in the application of behavioral economics (BE) to public policy from 2015 to 2025. It analyzes the field's institutionalization, the evolution of its core concepts, and the significant critiques that have shaped its modern trajectory.

Design/methodology/approach: This article is a comprehensive literature review, synthesizing findings from published academic papers, institutional reports, and meta-analyses. It systematically maps empirical findings across policy domains and critically examines ethical, methodological, and practical challenges.

Findings: The review finds that BE has matured from a novel tool into an established field. Mechanisms like defaults, framing, and friction reduction have been widely deployed with varying success. This period has also been defined by a critical reckoning with the replication crisis and ethical debates concerning autonomy. The field is responding by integrating with computational social science and artificial intelligence, moving toward more interdisciplinary and empowering approaches.

Originality/value: This review offers a nuanced, critical analysis of a pivotal decade in behavioral public policy. It moves beyond cataloging interventions to provide a coherent narrative of institutionalization, challenge, and adaptation. The paper concludes that the field's value lies in fostering a more realistic, evidence-based, and human-centric paradigm for policy design.

title: Defining Entrepreneurship Through Acquisition: An Empirical Classification Framework
affiliations: Florida Gulf Coast University, Florida Atlantic University, Florida Atlantic University and Case Western Reserve University

detail.title: Defining Entrepreneurship Through Acquisition: An Empirical Classification Framework
detail.abstract: Entrepreneurship through acquisition (ETA) is an emerging yet poorly defined mode of entrepreneurial entry. We analyze more than 15,000 U.S. business transactions and uncover consistent discontinuities in deal size, financing, and governance that empirically distinguish ETA from larger-scale acquisitions. These results provide the first operational framework for identifying ETA in archival and new data, enabling systematic research on this growing phenomenon. By grounding ETA in the opportunity-based tradition, we position acquisition as a parallel mode of entrepreneurial opportunity pursuit, offering scholars a replicable tool and practitioners clearer benchmarks for action.

title: Surrogate-driven Design Optimization with Uncertainty Constraints in Monte Carlo Simulations
affiliations: University of Michigan, Los Alamos National Laboratory, Los Alamos National Laboratory, Los Alamos National Laboratory and University of Michigan at Ann Arbor

detail.title: Surrogate-driven Design Optimization with Uncertainty Constraints in Monte Carlo Simulations
detail.abstract: In multi-objective design tasks, the computational cost increases rapidly when high-fidelity simulations are used to evaluate objective functions. Surrogate models help mitigate this cost by approximating the simulation output, simplifying the design process. However, under high uncertainty, surrogate models trained on noisy data can produce inaccurate predictions, as their performance depends heavily on the quality of training data. This study investigates the impact of data uncertainty on two multi-objective design problems modelled using Monte Carlo transport simulations: a neutron moderator and an ion-to-neutron converter. For each, a grid search was performed using five different tally uncertainty levels to generate training data for neural network surrogate models. These models were then optimized using NSGA-III. The recovered Pareto-fronts were analyzed across uncertainty levels, and the impact of training data quality on optimization outcomes was quantified. Average simulation times were also compared to evaluate the trade-off between accuracy and computational cost. Results show that the influence of simulation uncertainty is strongly problem-dependent. In the neutron moderator case, higher uncertainties led to exaggerated objective sensitivities and distorted Pareto-fronts, reducing normalized hypervolume. In contrast, the ion-to-neutron converter task was less affected—low-fidelity simulations produced results similar to those from high-fidelity data. These findings suggest that a fixed-fidelity approach is not optimal. Surrogate models can still recover the Pareto-front under noisy conditions, and multi-fidelity studies can help identify the appropriate uncertainty level for each problem, enabling better trade-offs between computational efficiency and optimization accuracy.

title: Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) Adoption in Agriculture: Determinants, Impact, and Policy Implications for Rural Development in Pakistan
affiliations: Jiangsu University, School of Management and MNS-University of Agriculture

detail.title: Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) Adoption in Agriculture: Determinants, Impact, and Policy Implications for Rural Development in Pakistan
detail.abstract: This study examines both the determinants and impacts of Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) adoption in smallholder agriculture, using survey data from 300 farmers in Punjab, Pakistan. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was applied to hypothesized drivers as relative advantage, compatibility, observability, data security, information quality, social influence, and cost of technology. The results show that all determinants significantly influence ICTs adoption, with relative advantage (F = 6.219, p < 0.05), compatibility (F = 5.652, p < 0.05), and observability (F = 5.998, p < 0.001) exerting the strongest effects. Data security, information quality, and social influence also contributed positively, while high technology costs emerged as a significant barrier (F = 7.212, p < 0.05). Moderation analysis revealed that participation in ICT training (F = 3.112, p < 0.05) and access to AI tools (F = 5.009, p < 0.05) strengthened adoption pathways. ICTs adoption was further found to significantly improve agricultural performance (F = 4.342, p < 0.05), with the structural model demonstrating good fit (SRMR = 0.075; NFI = 0.95).These results extend existing technology adoption frameworks by validating their applicability in the context of developing-country agriculture, while also integrating key moderating factors. The study underscores the transformative potential of ICTs for smallholder farming, highlighting the need for targeted policy interventions such as reducing technology costs, improving rural ICT infrastructure, and scaling up farmer training programs to accelerate digital inclusion and foster sustainable rural development.

title: Counterfactual image generation network based on gradient optimization and attribute interpolation
affiliations: Anhui University, Anhui University, Anhui University and Anhui University

detail.title: Counterfactual image generation network based on gradient optimization and attribute interpolation
detail.abstract: Counterfactual image generation operates through controllable modification of image attributes. This modification capability helps reveal the causal mechanism behind model predictions. However, existing methods exhibit limitations at both pixel and semantic levels, lead to shape distortion and semantic inconsistency because of   neglecting the interactive relationships between texture and background features. This paper proposes a novel counterfactual image generation network\text{(CIGGA)} based on  gradient optimization via attribute interpolation, Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence constraints and discriminative ensemble training. This approach enhances the fidelity and diversity of counterfactual samples. Experiments on the Morpho-MNIST dataset demonstrate that CIGN generates more reliable, accurate and dispersal counterfactual images, outperforms existing methods in terms of target class accuracy, distribution similarity and perceptual quality metrics.

title: Scientific Identification and Occurrence of Black Aphid (Aphis fabae) on Faba Bean in Central Ethiopia
affiliations: Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research

detail.title: Scientific Identification and Occurrence of Black Aphid (Aphis fabae) on Faba Bean in Central Ethiopia
detail.abstract: Field surveys conducted in central Ethiopia (March 12, 2024, at Alpha Alpha Animal Feeds, and August 2025 in faba bean fields) revealed significant infestations of black aphids (Aphis fabae). These surveys aimed to document pest occurrence, identify species, and assess crop damage in key faba bean production areas. Specimens were collected from tender shoots, flowers, and pods, preserved in 70% ethanol, and examined under stereomicroscopy. Morphological traits, including body color, cornicle presence, and wing venation, confirmed species identity. High population densities caused leaf curling, stunted growth, flower abortion, and pod deformation. Honeydew secretions promoted secondary sooty mold. These findings highlight the economic significance of A. fabae in central Ethiopian faba bean production and the need for integrated pest management strategies.
